results.name: CharacterModule.dual
results.source_text:
/--
Given an abelian group homomorphism `f : A → B`, `f⋆(L) := L ∘ f` defines a linear map
from `B⋆` to `A⋆`.
-/
@[simps] def dual (f : A →ₗ[R] B) : CharacterModule B →ₗ[R] CharacterModule A where
  toFun L := L.comp f.toAddMonoidHom
  map_add' := by aesop
  map_smul' r c := by ext x; exact congr(c $(f.map_smul r x)).symm
results.docstring:
Given an abelian group homomorphism `f : A → B`, `f⋆(L) := L ∘ f` defines a linear map
from `B⋆` to `A⋆`.

results.name: CharacterModule.dual_zero
results.source_text:
@[simp]
lemma dual_zero : dual (0 : A →ₗ[R] B) = 0 := by
  ext f
  exact map_zero f

results.name: Module.Dual
results.source_text:
/-- The left dual space of an R-module M is the R-module of linear maps `M → R`. -/
@[wikidata Q752487]
abbrev Dual (R M : Type*) [Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] :=
  M →ₗ[R] R
results.docstring: The left dual space of an R-module M is the R-module of linear maps `M → R`.

results.name: Submodule.dualAnnihilator
results.source_text:
/-- The `dualAnnihilator` of a submodule `W` is the set of linear maps `φ` such
  that `φ w = 0` for all `w ∈ W`. -/
def dualAnnihilator {R M : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M]
    (W : Submodule R M) : Submodule R <| Module.Dual R M :=
  LinearMap.ker W.dualRestrict
results.docstring:
The `dualAnnihilator` of a submodule `W` is the set of linear maps `φ` such
that `φ w = 0` for all `w ∈ W`.

results.name: WeakDual.characterSpace
results.source_text:
/-- The character space of a topological algebra is the subset of elements of the weak dual that
are also algebra homomorphisms. -/
def characterSpace (𝕜 : Type*) (A : Type*) [CommSemiring 𝕜] [TopologicalSpace 𝕜] [ContinuousAdd 𝕜]
    [ContinuousConstSMul 𝕜 𝕜] [NonUnitalNonAssocSemiring A] [TopologicalSpace A] [Module 𝕜 A] :=
  {φ : WeakDual 𝕜 A | φ ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ x y : A, φ (x * y) = φ x * φ y}
results.docstring:
The character space of a topological algebra is the subset of elements of the weak dual that
are also algebra homomorphisms.

results.name: minkowskiMatrix.dual
results.source_text:
/-- The dual of a matrix with respect to the Minkowski metric.
  A suitable name for this construction is the Minkowski dual. -/
def dual : Matrix (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) ℝ := η * Λᵀ * η
results.docstring:
The dual of a matrix with respect to the Minkowski metric.
A suitable name for this construction is the Minkowski dual.

results.name: minkowskiMatrix.dual_mul
results.source_text:
/-- The Minkowski dual swaps multiplications (acts contravariantly). -/
@[simp]
lemma dual_mul : dual (Λ * Λ') = dual Λ' * dual Λ := by
  simp only [dual, transpose_mul, ← mul_assoc]
  noncomm_ring [minkowskiMatrix.sq]
results.docstring: The Minkowski dual swaps multiplications (acts contravariantly).

results.name: Lorentz.contrContrContractField.dual_mulVec_left
results.source_text:
lemma dual_mulVec_left : ⟪dual Λ *ᵥ x, y⟫ₘ = ⟪x, Λ *ᵥ y⟫ₘ := by
  rw [symm, dual_mulVec_right, symm]

results.name: minkowskiMatrix.dual_dual
results.source_text:
/-- The Minkowski dual is involutive (i.e. `dual (dual Λ)) = Λ`). -/
@[simp]
lemma dual_dual : Function.Involutive (@dual d) := by
  intro Λ
  simp only [dual, transpose_mul, eq_transpose, transpose_transpose, ← mul_assoc]
  noncomm_ring [minkowskiMatrix.sq]
results.docstring: The Minkowski dual is involutive (i.e. `dual (dual Λ)) = Λ`).

results.name: MeasurableSpace
results.source_text:
/-- A measurable space is a space equipped with a σ-algebra. -/
@[class] structure MeasurableSpace (α : Type*) where
  /-- Predicate saying that a given set is measurable. Use `MeasurableSet` in the root namespace
  instead. -/
  MeasurableSet' : Set α → Prop
  /-- The empty set is a measurable set. Use `MeasurableSet.empty` instead. -/
  measurableSet_empty : MeasurableSet' ∅
  /-- The complement of a measurable set is a measurable set. Use `MeasurableSet.compl` instead. -/
  measurableSet_compl : ∀ s, MeasurableSet' s → MeasurableSet' sᶜ
  /-- The union of a sequence of measurable sets is a measurable set. Use a more general
  `MeasurableSet.iUnion` instead. -/
  measurableSet_iUnion : ∀ f : ℕ → Set α, (∀ i, MeasurableSet' (f i)) → MeasurableSet' (⋃ i, f i)
results.docstring: A measurable space is a space equipped with a σ-algebra.

results.name: MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace
results.source_text:
/-- A measure space is a measurable space equipped with a
  measure, referred to as `volume`. -/
class MeasureSpace (α : Type*) extends MeasurableSpace α where
  volume : Measure α
results.docstring:
A measure space is a measurable space equipped with a
measure, referred to as `volume`.

results.name: MeasurableSpace.ext_iff
iInter_halfSpaces_eq
results.source_text:
/-- A closed convex set is the intersection of the half-spaces containing it. -/
theorem iInter_halfSpaces_eq (hs₁ : Convex ℝ s) (hs₂ : IsClosed s) :
    ⋂ l : StrongDual ℝ E, { x | ∃ y ∈ s, l x ≤ l y } = s := by
  rw [Set.iInter_setOf]
  refine Set.Subset.antisymm (fun x hx => ?_) fun x hx l => ⟨x, hx, le_rfl⟩
  by_contra h
  obtain ⟨l, s, hlA, hl⟩ := geometric_hahn_banach_closed_point hs₁ hs₂ h
  obtain ⟨y, hy, hxy⟩ := hx l
  exact ((hxy.trans_lt (hlA y hy)).trans hl).not_ge le_rfl
results.docstring: A closed convex set is the intersection of the half-spaces containing it.

results.name: MeasurableSpace.copy
results.source_text:
/-- Copy of a `MeasurableSpace` with a new `MeasurableSet` equal to the old one. Useful to fix
definitional equalities. -/
@[implicit_reducible]
protected def copy (m : MeasurableSpace α) (p : Set α → Prop) (h : ∀ s, p s ↔ MeasurableSet[m] s) :
    MeasurableSpace α where
  MeasurableSet' := p
  measurableSet_empty := by simpa only [h] using! m.measurableSet_empty
  measurableSet_compl := by simpa only [h] using! m.measurableSet_compl
  measurableSet_iUnion := by simpa only [h] using! m.measurableSet_iUnion
results.docstring:
Copy of a `MeasurableSpace` with a new `MeasurableSet` equal to the old one. Useful to fix
definitional equalities.

results.name: Space.instModuleReal
results.source_text:
instance {d} : Module ℝ (Space d) where
  one_smul x := by
    ext i
    simp
  mul_smul a b x := by
    ext i
    simp [mul_assoc]
  smul_add a x y := by
    ext i
    simp [mul_add]
  smul_zero a := by
    ext i
    simp
  add_smul a b x := by
    ext i
    simp [add_mul]
  zero_smul x := by
    ext i
    simp

  `($[$doc?]? $[$attrs?]? def $name : InformalDefinition $body:declVal)

should outline its mathematical or physical content and specify useful references. Use the attribute
`note_attr_informal` from `Physlib.Meta.Notes.Basic` to mark the informal definition as a note.

results.name: Informal.constantInfoToInformalDefinition
results.source_text:
/-- Takes a `ConstantInfo` corresponding to a `InformalDefinition` and returns
  the corresponding `InformalDefinition`. -/
unsafe def constantInfoToInformalDefinition (c : ConstantInfo) : CoreM InformalDefinition := do
  match c with
  | .defnInfo c => evalConstCheck InformalDefinition ``InformalDefinition c.name
  | _ => panic!
    "Passed constantInfoToInformalDefinition a `ConstantInfo` that is not a `InformalDefinition`"
results.docstring:
Takes a `ConstantInfo` corresponding to a `InformalDefinition` and returns
the corresponding `InformalDefinition`.
